c2224532.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 130 of 2023): judges can request transfers or swap posts with colleagues in other courts of the same branch, state, federal or labor.

c407657.titulo: Creates a fund to revitalize the São Francisco River
c407657.oQueMuda: Creates a fund to restore the environment and develop the São Francisco River basin.
c407657.quemAfeta: Residents of the São Francisco basin.
c407657.porQueImporta: Today revitalizing the São Francisco River depends on federal programs with funding set each year. Under the PEC, there would be a fund with money reserved for the basin.

c483817.titulo: Makes the Cerrado and the Caatinga national heritage
c483817.oQueMuda: These two biomes would be added to the national heritage areas.
c483817.quemAfeta: Residents and producers in the Cerrado and the Caatinga.
c483817.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution lists as national heritage the Amazon, Atlantic Forest, Serra do Mar, Mato Grosso Pantanal and the coastal zone. Under the PEC, the Cerrado and Caatinga would be added, with use conditioned on preservation.

s8569449.oQueMuda: The federal government would top up the Municipal Participation Fund to keep the same share of GDP as in 2022.
s8569449.porQueImporta: Today FPM varies with income tax and IPI revenue, and falls when revenue falls. Under the PEC, the federal government would top it up to keep it at the same share of GDP as in 2022.

c398998.titulo: Ends the constitutional fifth and political appointments to courts
c398998.oQueMuda:
The constitutional fifth would end: seats reserved for lawyers and prosecutors in courts would go to career judges.
Supreme Court justices would be chosen from among Superior Court of Justice justices, alternating seniority and merit, with no presidential nomination or Senate approval.
The Superior Court of Justice, regional courts and other courts would choose their own members.
Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) ministers would be chosen by the court itself from among its auditors.
c398998.porQueImporta: Today a fifth of the seats in several courts go to lawyers and prosecutors, and Supreme Court, Superior Court of Justice and TCU members are appointed by the president or Congress. Under the PEC, these choices would stay within the careers themselves.

s7720809.titulo: Guarantees a full public health team for pregnant women
s7720809.oQueMuda: The public health system (SUS) would have to provide a pediatrician, gynecologist, obstetrician, nurses and psychologist during prenatal care, birth and postpartum.
s7720809.porQueImporta: Today the public health system offers prenatal care and childbirth, but the team varies by place. Under the PEC, it would have to guarantee a pediatrician, gynecologist, obstetrician, nurses and psychologist for prenatal care, birth and postpartum.

c2092664.titulo: Reserves 10% of individual amendments for public safety
c2092664.oQueMuda: 10% of legislators' individual budget amendments would go to public safety.
c2092664.porQueImporta: Today half of individual budget amendments must go to health, and the rest is free. Under the PEC, 10% would have to go to public security.

s8242831.titulo: Allows public and private companies to collect and process plasma
s8242831.oQueMuda: Today the Constitution bans all trade in organs, tissues, blood and blood products. The text approved by the Senate Justice Committee opens a single exception: human plasma could be collected, processed and sold by public and private institutions, for research and to make medicines intended preferably for SUS. The private sector would act in a complementary way, when requested by the Health Ministry. The rules would be set by law.
s8242831.quemAfeta: Blood donors, patients who depend on plasma-derived medicines, the state company Hemobrás and companies in the sector.
s8242831.porQueImporta: Today plasma donated in Brazil is processed by the state company Hemobrás, and blood donation has been voluntary and unpaid since the 1980s. Under the PEC, plasma could be traded.
s8242831.nota: The National Health Council, the Health Ministry and Hemobrás oppose it and say that trading plasma could reduce voluntary blood donations. The Brazilian Hematology Association supports the PEC and says Hemobrás meets only about 10% of the country's immunoglobulin needs.

s8442337.oQueMuda: Sets institutional rules for the prosecutors who work with the Courts of Accounts.
s8442337.quemAfeta: Audit prosecutors and Courts of Accounts.
s8442337.porQueImporta: Today the Audit Prosecutor's Office, which works in the Audit Courts, has few rules in the Constitution. Under the PEC, it would gain its own institutional rules, such as autonomy and guarantees for its members.

s8549385.titulo: Extends the right to life to the unborn
s8549385.oQueMuda: The right to life would protect the embryo from conception.
s8549385.porQueImporta: Today abortion is allowed in Brazil in cases of rape, risk to the mother's life and fetal anencephaly, rules set by the Penal Code and a Supreme Court ruling. Under the PEC, the Constitution, which ranks above those rules, would say the right to life protects the embryo from conception.

c406708.titulo: Sets aside budget money for affordable housing
c406708.oQueMuda: Federal, state and city governments would have to allocate fixed funds to social housing funds.
c406708.quemAfeta: Families without adequate housing and governments.
c406708.porQueImporta: Today affordable housing programs depend on each year's budget. Under the PEC, the federal government, states and municipalities would have to allocate fixed funds to social housing funds.

s8513795.titulo: Alternative tax reform with a financial transactions tax
s8513795.oQueMuda:
## Financial transactions tax
The federal government would create a tax on financial transfers and transactions, similar to the former CPMF.
Once in force, the IOF, the rural land tax (ITR), the provision for a wealth tax, employers' and workers' social security contributions, the education payroll levy and contributions to the S System would be abolished.
All Cide contributions, such as the fuel one, would be abolished.
## State consumption tax
The ICMS would be replaced, from the seventh year, by a state tax on goods and services, shared between states and the Federal District and managed by a committee.
The IPI would end after a transition period.
s8513795.porQueImporta: The tax reform enacted in 2023 followed another model: it replaced ICMS and ISS with the IBS and PIS/Cofins with the CBS, with no financial transactions tax. This PEC proposed an alternative model that swaps payroll and revenue contributions for a tax on transactions.

s8545103.titulo: Bans charging union fees to non-members
s8545103.oQueMuda: Unions could only charge any contribution to non-member workers or companies with each one's prior individual authorization.
s8545103.porQueImporta: In 2023 the Supreme Court allowed unions to charge an assistance contribution to all workers in the profession, including non-members, as long as they can opt out. Under the PEC, charging non-members would require prior individual authorization.

s8539271.titulo: Requires Supreme Court justices to face a new hearing every 8 years
s8539271.oQueMuda: Every 8 years in office, Supreme Court justices would undergo a new public hearing in the Senate, which would vote on their reappointment by absolute majority.
s8539271.quemAfeta: Supreme Court justices and the Senate.
s8539271.porQueImporta: Today Supreme Court justices are questioned by the Senate only before taking office and stay until 75. Under the PEC, every 8 years the Senate would decide whether they stay.

s8538765.titulo: Temporarily raises transfers to the FPM
s8538765.oQueMuda: The share of Income Tax and IPI going to the Municipal Participation Fund would rise by 2 percentage points for 24 months; from the 13th month, the increase would be cut in half.
s8538765.porQueImporta: Today the federal government transfers 22.5% of income tax and IPI to FPM, plus extra shares in July, September and December. Under the PEC, this share would increase for a period.

s8540424.titulo: Bars judges from cases handled by relatives' law firms
s8540424.oQueMuda: Judges could not rule on cases with lawyers who are their spouses or close relatives.
s8540424.porQueImporta: In 2023 the Supreme Court struck down the Civil Procedure Code rule barring judges from cases involving law firms of relatives. Under the PEC, this bar would be in the Constitution.

s7723044.titulo: Guarantees cities the ICMS and IPVA that states fail to pass on
s7723044.oQueMuda: The federal government would withhold state funds and pay cities directly the share of ICMS and IPVA not passed on.
s7723044.porQueImporta: Today states must pass 25% of ICMS and 50% of IPVA to city governments, and there are cases of delay. Under the PEC, the federal government would withhold state money and pay cities directly what was not transferred.

s8326366.titulo: Guarantees free public transit on election day
s8326366.oQueMuda: Buses, boats and intercity transport would be free on voting days.
s8326366.porQueImporta: Since 2023, under a Supreme Court ruling, cities with public transport must offer free rides on election days. Under the PEC, free buses, boats and intercity transport would be in the Constitution.

c2223558.titulo: Exempts Brazilian-made musical instruments from taxes
c2223558.oQueMuda: Musical instruments made in Brazil would be tax-free.
c2223558.porQueImporta: Today musical instruments pay taxes like other products. Under the PEC, those made in Brazil would be tax-free.

c2225811.oQueMuda: Creates a new case in which Brazilians who naturalize through marriage keep their nationality.
c2225811.porQueImporta: This PEC was shelved; in 2023 Amendment 131 already guaranteed that Brazilians who acquire another nationality, including through marriage, do not lose Brazilian nationality.

s8520995.titulo: Changes how Congress's internal rules are amended
s8520995.oQueMuda:
Bills creating or changing the internal rules of the Chamber, the Senate or Congress would have to be filed by one-third of members.
If not voted on within 30 days, they would block the house's agenda until voted, except for matters with a constitutional deadline.
s8520995.porQueImporta: Today the Chamber and Senate change their internal rules by resolution, approved only by that house. Under the PEC, there would be rules in the Constitution for these votes.

c1555497.titulo: Adds internet access and message privacy to the fundamental rights
c1555497.oQueMuda: Guarantees everyone internet access and the confidentiality of digital communications, which could only be broken by court order in criminal investigations. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c1555497.quemAfeta: Internet users, technology companies and the police.
c1555497.porQueImporta: Confidentiality of communications is already in the Constitution; the change mentions the internet explicitly.

s8513844.titulo: Guarantees free transit for low-income people with disabilities
s8513844.oQueMuda: Low-income people with disabilities would ride urban public transit for free.
s8513844.quemAfeta: People with disabilities and city governments.
s8513844.porQueImporta: Today free transport for people with disabilities depends on each city's or state's laws. Under the PEC, low-income people with disabilities would ride urban public transport free nationwide.

c1738814.oQueMuda: Guarantees extra operating time for lottery outlet permits.
c1738814.porQueImporta: Already in force: lottery outlet permits received additional operating time before a new tender.

s8488965.titulo: Changes the process for provisional measures
s8488965.oQueMuda:
Provisional measures would lapse if any stage missed its deadline: 40 days for the joint committee report, 40 days for the Chamber vote, 30 in the Senate and 10 for the Chamber to review Senate changes.
Deadlines would pause during recess.
If the Chamber or Senate did not vote within 30 and 20 days, the measure would block the house's agenda.
Reissuing in the same legislative session the content of a measure that was rejected or lapsed would be banned.
s8488965.porQueImporta: Today a provisional measure is valid for up to 120 days and blocks Congress's agenda after 45. Under the PEC, these deadlines, the agenda block and reissue rules would change.

s8489404.titulo: Makes the Caatinga, Cerrado and Pampa national heritage
s8489404.oQueMuda: These three biomes would be added to the national heritage areas.
s8489404.quemAfeta: Residents and producers in these biomes.
s8489404.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution lists as national heritage the Amazon, Atlantic Forest, Serra do Mar, Mato Grosso Pantanal and the coastal zone. Under the PEC, the Caatinga, Cerrado and Pampa would be added, with use conditioned on preservation.

c2118343.titulo: Limits civil servants' vacation to 30 days
c2118343.oQueMuda: All public employees would have 30 days of vacation a year, with one-third extra pay.
c2118343.quemAfeta: Civil servants, including judges and prosecutors.
c2118343.porQueImporta: Today judges, prosecutors and some other careers have 60 days of vacation a year, while other civil servants have 30. Under the PEC, all would have 30 days.

c139244.titulo: Direct election of state attorneys general
c139244.oQueMuda: The heads of state prosecutors' offices would be elected by prosecutors themselves.
c139244.porQueImporta: Today the governor chooses the head of the state prosecution service from a list of three names voted by prosecutors. Under the PEC, the prosecutors' top choice would become head, without the governor choosing.

c2152285.titulo: Creates a democracy fund financed by politicians' salaries
c2152285.oQueMuda: Politicians and appointees would pay a contribution on their salaries to a fund financing democracy.
c2152285.quemAfeta: Elected politicians and holders of appointed posts.
c2152285.porQueImporta: Today campaigns are paid mainly by the public election fund and by individual donations. Under the PEC, politicians and appointees would pay a contribution on their salaries to a democracy financing fund.

s8472168.titulo: Puts mental integrity and algorithm transparency into the Constitution
s8472168.oQueMuda: States that scientific and technological development must ensure people's mental integrity and the transparency of algorithms, as set by law. On its own, it does not create rules for companies: a law is needed.
s8472168.quemAfeta: Technology users, digital companies and lawmakers.
s8472168.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution does not address mental integrity or algorithms. Under the PEC, these topics would join the list of fundamental rights, to be regulated by law.

c1050543.titulo: Allows seizing assets from crime or corruption
c1050543.oQueMuda: Prosecutors and government attorneys could ask courts to seize assets from crime, misconduct or illicit enrichment.
c1050543.quemAfeta: People with assets of illicit origin.
c1050543.porQueImporta: Today forfeiture of crime-related assets generally depends on a criminal conviction. Under the PEC, prosecutors and government attorneys could ask courts to seize illicit assets in a separate action.

s7857865.titulo: Adds climate stability to the principles of the economy
s7857865.oQueMuda: The economic order would have to seek climate stability and the government would have to act against climate change.
s7857865.porQueImporta: Today the principles of the economic order include environmental protection but do not mention climate. Under the PEC, climate stability would be added, and governments would have a duty to act against climate change.

c427297.titulo: Guarantees night-shift pay to police and firefighters
c427297.oQueMuda: Military police, firefighters and other security agents would be entitled to night-shift pay.
c427297.porQueImporta: Today formal workers and civilian civil servants get a night-shift bonus, but military police and firefighters have no such right in the Constitution. Under the PEC, they would.

c1278930.titulo: Sets working hours for military police and firefighters
c1278930.oQueMuda: Military police and firefighters' working hours could not exceed 40 hours a week, with schedule offsetting allowed. The rule would not apply during intervention, state of defense, state of siege or public calamity.
c1278930.porQueImporta: Today there is no working-hours limit in the Constitution for military police and firefighters. Under the PEC, there would be maximum daily and weekly hours for them.

c2092228.titulo: Places notary offices among the functions essential to justice
c2092228.oQueMuda: Notaries and registrars would get their own section in the Constitution.
c2092228.porQueImporta: Today notary offices are mentioned in the Constitution only in one article on notarial services. Under the PEC, they would get their own section among the functions essential to justice, alongside lawyers, public defenders and prosecutors.

s5073365.oQueMuda:
A National Sports Fund (Fundesporte) would be created to broaden access to sports.
The fund would receive an extra half percentage point of IPI, or of the tax replacing it, on foods of low nutritional quality.
States and the Federal District would have to create sports funds, with management including civil society, and could charge up to half a point more ICMS on those foods.
s5073365.porQueImporta: Today sport receives money from each year's budget and part of lottery revenue. Under the PEC, there would be a dedicated national fund.

s7975882.titulo: Extends book tax exemption to digital formats
s7975882.oQueMuda: Books, newspapers and magazines, including digital ones, would be free from all taxes.
s7975882.porQueImporta: Today printed books, newspapers and magazines pay no taxes, and the Supreme Court extended this to e-books in 2017. Under the PEC, all of them, printed or digital, would be free of all taxes, including contributions.

s7986137.titulo: Adds internet access to the fundamental and social rights
s7986137.oQueMuda: States that the State must guarantee internet access to all residents, adds internet access to the social rights and tells a law to guarantee net neutrality and quality. On its own, it does not create programs or funding: a law is needed.
s7986137.quemAfeta: People without internet access, telecom companies and governments.
s7986137.porQueImporta: The Brazilian Internet Bill of Rights already treats access as essential; the change raises it to a right in the Constitution.

s7987247.titulo: Repeals the spending cap and creates spending targets
s7987247.oQueMuda: Repeals the spending cap amendment and sets spending targets in the multi-year plan, with extra spending in 2021 and 2022.
s7987247.quemAfeta: The federal government and social program recipients.
s7987247.porQueImporta: This 2020 PEC proposed ending the spending cap created in 2016. The cap was eventually replaced in 2023 by another fiscal rule.
s7987247.apelido: End of the Spending Cap PEC

s8448291.titulo: Creates an income-based contribution to repay student loans
s8448291.oQueMuda: Allows a tax so former students repay their loans according to future income.
s8448291.quemAfeta: Students who use loans such as Fies.
s8448291.porQueImporta: Today Fies student loans are repaid in fixed installments after graduation, under contract rules. Under the PEC, a tax could be created so former students repay according to income.

c323818.titulo: Splits oil and mining royalties by population and HDI
c323818.oQueMuda:
Royalties from oil, gas, hydropower and minerals would go to a fund: 12% to federal agencies linked to extraction, 33% to states and 55% to municipalities.
Among states and municipalities, the split would consider population, area and, with the greatest weight, the HDI: the lower the HDI, the larger the share.
c323818.quemAfeta: States and cities, producers or not.
c323818.porQueImporta: Today most oil and mining royalties go to the states and municipalities where extraction occurs. Under the PEC, they would be split among all by population, area and HDI.

c1049154.titulo: Adds access to energy to the social rights
c1049154.oQueMuda: Adds 'access to energy' to the list of social rights. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c1049154.quemAfeta: People without electricity, low-income consumers and governments.
c1049154.porQueImporta: Today access to energy is not on the list of social rights, and programs such as the social electricity rate exist by law. Under the PEC, it would be added to that list.

c1230264.titulo: Increases the share of income tax and IPI sent to cities
c1230264.oQueMuda: The extra share of Income Tax and IPI paid to the Municipal Participation Fund in July would rise from 1% to 2%, increasing by 0.5 point a year.
c1230264.porQueImporta: Today the federal government transfers 22.5% of income tax and IPI to FPM, plus extra shares in July, September and December. Under the PEC, this share would increase.

c2075915.titulo: Adds internet access to the fundamental rights
c2075915.oQueMuda: Adds to the list of fundamental rights: 'universal internet access is guaranteed to everyone'. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2075915.quemAfeta: People without internet access and governments.
c2075915.porQueImporta: The Brazilian Internet Bill of Rights already treats access as essential; the change raises it to a fundamental right.

c2088568.titulo: Adds support for women victims of violence to social assistance
c2088568.oQueMuda: Social assistance would aim to support women who are victims of violence.
c2088568.porQueImporta: Today the goals of social assistance in the Constitution include protecting families, childhood and old age. Under the PEC, support for women victims of violence would be added.

c2198865.titulo: Updates the wording to 'person with a disability'
c2198865.oQueMuda: The Constitution would use the phrase 'person with a disability' throughout.
c2198865.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution uses terms such as 'person bearing a disability'. Under the PEC, it would use 'person with a disability', without changing rights.

s7834640.titulo: Restricts appeals to the Supreme Court in criminal cases
s7834640.oQueMuda: Extraordinary appeals to the Supreme Court would no longer be allowed in criminal matters.
s7834640.quemAfeta: Criminal defendants and the Supreme Court.
s7834640.porQueImporta: Today criminal defendants can appeal to the Supreme Court when they claim a constitutional violation. Under the PEC, this appeal would no longer exist in criminal cases.

s7933328.oQueMuda: The government would have to encourage payments to those who preserve nature and create jobs in environmental activities.
s7933328.porQueImporta: Since 2021 a law has created the National Policy on Payment for Environmental Services. Under the PEC, governments would have a constitutional duty to encourage these payments.

s7959745.titulo: Requires a list of three to choose the Prosecutor General
s7959745.oQueMuda: The President would choose the Prosecutor General from a list drawn up by federal prosecutors.
s7959745.porQueImporta: Today the president freely chooses the Prosecutor General among career prosecutors, with Senate approval. Under the PEC, the choice would have to come from a list of three names voted by prosecutors.

s8323670.titulo: Gives the Supreme Court jurisdiction over crimes against democracy
s8323670.oQueMuda: Crimes against the democratic rule of law would be tried directly by the Supreme Court.
s8323670.quemAfeta: People accused of these crimes and the Supreme Court.
s8323670.porQueImporta: Today crimes against the democratic rule of law are tried by federal courts, unless defendants have special jurisdiction at the Supreme Court. Under the PEC, all such crimes would be tried directly by the Supreme Court.

s7899802.titulo: Creates a fund to fight child poverty
s7899802.oQueMuda: Creates a fund with child poverty reduction targets and rewards for governments that make progress.
s7899802.porQueImporta: Today child poverty is addressed through programs such as Bolsa Família. Under the PEC, there would be a fund with child poverty reduction targets and rewards for governments that meet them.

s7901820.titulo: Creates guarantee funds for small businesses
s7901820.oQueMuda:
A Solidarity Guarantee Fund would be created to guarantee loans for micro, small and medium businesses at banks and development institutions.
Its initial capital would be R$ 2.5 billion in federal money and R$ 5 billion in government bonds or shares of state companies.
Regional incentives would include guarantee funds for investments in the regions.
s7901820.porQueImporta: Today there are guarantee funds created by law, such as Pronampe's. Under the PEC, there would be regional funds in the Constitution to guarantee loans to micro, small and medium businesses.

s7905790.titulo: Exempts donations to NGOs and research institutes from tax
s7905790.oQueMuda: Donations and bequests to nonprofit organizations would not pay the inheritance and gift tax (ITCMD).
s7905790.porQueImporta: Today donations and inheritances pay ITCMD, a state tax, except for each state's exemptions. Under the PEC, those made to non-profits and research institutes would be exempt nationwide.

s7916284.titulo: Postponed the 2020 municipal elections because of the pandemic
s7916284.oQueMuda: Allowed the Superior Electoral Court to postpone the 2020 elections and set terms to unify elections from 2026.
s7916284.porQueImporta: The 2020 municipal elections were postponed to November by another PEC, which became Amendment 107. This proposal, besides the postponement, set terms to unify elections from 2026.

s7917387.titulo: Unifies elections by extending municipal terms
s7917387.oQueMuda: Mayors and council members elected in 2016 would serve 6-year terms to coincide with other elections.
s7917387.porQueImporta: Today municipal and general elections alternate every two years. Under the PEC, mayors and councilors elected in 2016 would have 6-year terms, with no election in 2020, to unify the calendar.

s7917934.titulo: Counts pandemic work time double for retirement
s7917934.oQueMuda: Public health and security workers who fought COVID-19 would have that time counted double for retirement.
s7917934.porQueImporta: Today each year worked counts once toward retirement. Under the PEC, health and security civil servants who worked during the pandemic would have that time counted double.

c104989.titulo: Lets seconded civil servants transfer permanently
c104989.oQueMuda: Permanent civil servants who have worked for more than three consecutive years, on secondment, at another agency could choose, within 90 days, to stay permanently at the agency where they are.
c104989.quemAfeta: Civil servants on loan to other bodies.
c104989.porQueImporta: Today seconded civil servants remain in their original post, and changing posts requires a public exam. Under the PEC, they could stay permanently in the body where they work.

s8077867.titulo: Extends pension debt installment plans to 240 months
s8077867.oQueMuda: Governments could pay debts to their employees' pension systems in up to 240 installments during the pandemic.
s8077867.quemAfeta: States, cities and their civil servants.
s8077867.porQueImporta: Today governments with debts to their civil servants' pension funds have shorter installment periods. Under the PEC, they could pay these debts in up to 240 months, or 20 years.

s8078289.titulo: Bans tax increases during the pandemic
s8078289.oQueMuda:
While a national pandemic calamity lasted and less than 60% of the population was vaccinated, the federal government, states and municipalities could not create taxes, raise rates, change tax bases to collect more or cut tax exemptions and incentives.
Changes to raise money used only to fight the calamity would be exempt.
s8078289.porQueImporta: Today governments can create or raise taxes during disasters, following normal timing rules. Under the PEC, this would be banned during the disaster, except to fight it.

s8097900.titulo: Extends pension debt installment plans until 2021
s8097900.oQueMuda: Extends installment plans for governments' pension debts to 240 months and allows debt forgiveness.
s8097900.quemAfeta: States, cities and their civil servants.
s8097900.porQueImporta: Today governments with pension debts have shorter installment periods and cannot have debts forgiven. Under the PEC, the period would be up to 240 months and part of the debts would be forgiven.

s8099954.titulo: Creates quotas for Black candidates and by gender in the legislature
s8099954.oQueMuda: Sets minimum shares of candidates of each gender and of Black people, and reserves campaign funds and TV time for them.
s8099954.quemAfeta: Parties, women candidates and Black candidates.
s8099954.porQueImporta: Today the law requires each party to have at least 30% women candidates, and the Constitution reserves 30% of funds for women. Under the PEC, there would also be minimums for Black candidates, with reserved funds and TV time.

s8113511.titulo: Creates the Opportunities Amendment with a minimum income
s8113511.oQueMuda: Guarantees a minimum income and reserves budget money to expand early education and other opportunities.
s8113511.porQueImporta: Today income and early education programs depend on laws and each year's budget. Under the PEC, there would be a guaranteed minimum income and resources reserved in the Constitution to expand early education.

s8138727.titulo: Sends the top three candidates to the runoff
s8138727.oQueMuda: If no one wins a majority in the first round, the three top candidates would compete in the second.
s8138727.quemAfeta: Voters and candidates for president, governor and mayor.
s8138727.porQueImporta: Today, if no one gets more than half of the valid votes, the top two go to a runoff. Under the PEC, the top three would compete in the runoff.

s8154053.titulo: Changes the ICMS on fuel, gas and electricity
s8154053.oQueMuda:
The ICMS on fuels would have a maximum rate of 10% of the transaction value, and on cooking gas, 1%.
The ICMS on electricity would be set jointly by the states and capped at 10%.
s8154053.porQueImporta: Since 2022, fuel and energy have been treated as essential goods with capped ICMS rates. Under the PEC, the way ICMS is charged on oil products, cooking gas and electricity would change.

s8154081.titulo: Bans using the science fund to pay debt
s8154081.oQueMuda: Money from the National Science and Technology Development Fund could not be used to pay down the public debt.
s8154081.porQueImporta: Today part of idle federal fund money can be used to pay public debt. Under the PEC, FNDCT money, the main science fund, could not be used this way.

s8158286.titulo: Creates a national career for public health system doctors
s8158286.oQueMuda: Creates a national career for doctors in the public health system (SUS), with set requirements and pay.
s8158286.quemAfeta: Doctors and patients of the SUS.
s8158286.porQueImporta: Today public health system doctors are hired mostly by city and state governments, each with their own rules. Under the PEC, there would be a national SUS medical career with defined requirements and salary.

s8163561.titulo: Creates Auxílio Brasil and transparency rules for amendments
s8163561.oQueMuda: Replaces Bolsa Família with Auxílio Brasil and requires transparency in carrying out legislators' amendments.
s8163561.porQueImporta: In 2021 Bolsa Família was replaced by Auxílio Brasil, by law, and was renamed Bolsa Família again in 2023. This PEC dealt with that change and with transparency in budget amendment spending.

s8166899.titulo: Makes basic income a social right
s8166899.oQueMuda: Guarantees income to vulnerable families and creates fiscal exceptions to pay for the benefit.
s8166899.porQueImporta: Today Bolsa Família exists by law and depends on each year's budget. Under the PEC, basic income would be a social right, and the benefit would have exceptions to fiscal rules so it can be paid.

s8167542.titulo: Sends part of legislators' amendments to fighting poverty
s8167542.oQueMuda: Part of individual budget amendments would have to go to anti-poverty actions.
s8167542.porQueImporta: Today half of individual budget amendments must go to health, and the rest is free. Under the PEC, a share would have to go to anti-poverty actions.

s7752094.titulo: Applies the salary cap to organizations receiving public money
s7752094.oQueMuda: Nonprofits funded with public resources, such as the 'S System' training bodies, would have to respect the salary cap.
s7752094.quemAfeta: Directors and staff of these organizations.
s7752094.porQueImporta: Today the salary cap applies to public service, but not to bodies such as the 'Sistema S', funded by mandatory contributions. Under the PEC, salaries at these bodies would also have to respect the cap.

s8436103.titulo: Expands the Federal Public Defender's budget
s8436103.oQueMuda: The Federal Public Defender's Office would get yearly increases in its spending limit for 10 years.
s8436103.quemAfeta: People who rely on public defenders, and the defenders.
s8436103.porQueImporta: In 2014 the Constitution set an eight-year deadline for public defenders in every judicial district, a goal the Federal Public Defender's Office did not meet. Under the PEC, its spending limit would rise each year for 10 years.

s8436730.oQueMuda:
Medicines for human use would be immune from taxes.
The immunity would be phased in, with a 20% tax cut in the first year and another 20% each year, until reaching 100%.
s8436730.porQueImporta: Today medicines pay taxes, though some have reduced rates; under the tax reform, many will have a 60% reduction or exemption. Under the PEC, all human medicines would be tax-free.

s8437557.titulo: Adds a Federal District appeals judge to the CNJ
s8437557.oQueMuda: The National Council of Justice would gain an appeals judge from the Federal District Court of Justice.
s8437557.quemAfeta: The Federal District courts and the CNJ.
s8437557.porQueImporta: Today the CNJ has one appellate judge from a state Court of Justice, chosen by the Supreme Court from all states. Under the PEC, there would be an extra seat reserved for the Federal District Court of Justice.

c2084043.titulo: Makes spending on agricultural research mandatory
c2084043.oQueMuda: The government would have to carry out budget funds for scientific research in agriculture and livestock.
c2084043.porQueImporta: Today the budget for agricultural research, such as Embrapa's, can be frozen by the government. Under the PEC, spending it would be mandatory.

s8305239.titulo: Gives special retirement to municipal guards
s8305239.oQueMuda: Municipal guards would join the list of servants who may have, through each government's complementary law, different age and contribution time to retire, as already happens with police officers and prison and juvenile detention officers.
s8305239.porQueImporta: Today municipal guards follow general civil service retirement rules. Under the PEC, they would have special retirement at a lower age.

s8306962.titulo: Raises the March FPM transfer by 1%
s8306962.oQueMuda: The federal government would hand an extra 1% of its revenue to the Municipal Participation Fund every March.
s8306962.porQueImporta: Today the federal government transfers 22.5% of income tax and IPI to FPM, plus extra shares in July, September and December. Under the PEC, there would be another 1% in March.

s8319791.oQueMuda: Every Brazilian living in the country and every foreigner living there for at least five years, as well as migrants and refugees, aged over 18, would be entitled to a basic citizen income, paid as an ongoing benefit, regardless of income.
s8319791.porQueImporta: Since 2004 a law has provided for a citizen's basic income, which was never implemented. Under the PEC, there would be a basic income benefit in the Constitution, with defined funding sources.

s8320782.titulo: Bans selling state-owned companies between election and inauguration
s8320782.oQueMuda:
Between the election and the inauguration of a new government, selling public assets, including control of state-owned and mixed-capital companies, would be banned.
The ban would not apply when the head of the Executive is re-elected.
s8320782.porQueImporta: Today there is no ban on selling state companies or public assets between the election and the new government's inauguration. Under the PEC, this would be banned in that period.

s8331055.titulo: Creates an integrity system and anti-corruption courts
s8331055.oQueMuda: Establishes an integrity system in the judiciary and specialized courts for crimes against public administration.
s8331055.quemAfeta: Courts and defendants in corruption cases.
s8331055.porQueImporta: Today corruption crimes are tried by ordinary or federal criminal courts. Under the PEC, there would be courts specialized in these crimes and an integrity system in the judiciary.

s8332695.titulo: Gives Congress the say on suspending legislators' social media
s8332695.oQueMuda: Only the Chamber and the Senate could suspend or remove their members' online profiles and channels.
s8332695.porQueImporta: Today courts can order lawmakers' social media profiles suspended, as happened in Supreme Court investigations. Under the PEC, only the Chamber or Senate could do so.

s8291388.titulo: Creates an ombudsman against harassment and violence toward women in public service
s8291388.oQueMuda:
The federal government would have to create the National Women's Ombudsman, linked to the Executive, to prevent and fight harassment and violence against women within public administration in all branches, at federal, state and municipal level.
It would be headed by a tenured female civil servant, appointed by the president after Senate approval, for a fixed term.
s8291388.porQueImporta: Today each public body handles harassment cases on its own, through internal affairs offices and committees. Under the PEC, there would be a national body for these cases in public service.

s8293254.titulo: Creates binding precedents for the Superior Court of Justice
s8293254.oQueMuda: The Superior Court of Justice could issue precedents all judges would have to follow.
s8293254.quemAfeta: Judges, lawyers and parties to cases.
s8293254.porQueImporta: Today only the Supreme Court can issue binding precedents that all judges must follow. Under the PEC, the Superior Court of Justice could too, on federal law questions.

c2351680.oQueMuda: General pardons forgiving more than one-fifth of the remaining sentence would be banned, except for humanitarian pardons.
c2351680.porQueImporta: Today the president can grant pardons by decree, with bans only for heinous crimes, torture, trafficking and terrorism. Under the PEC, there would be new criteria and prohibitions.

s7741352.titulo: Raises the share of income tax and IPI sent to states to 26%
s7741352.oQueMuda: The share of income tax and IPI for the State Participation Fund would rise by 4.5 points.
s7741352.quemAfeta: State governments and the federal government.
s7741352.porQueImporta: Today the State Participation Fund receives 21.5% of income tax and IPI. Under the PEC, it would receive 26%, and the federal government would keep less.

s8402530.titulo: Adds the Federal Waterway Police to public safety
s8402530.oQueMuda: The Federal Waterway Police would become part of the public safety system.
s8402530.quemAfeta: Residents of river regions and the Federal Police.
s8402530.porQueImporta: Today policing on federal rivers is done mainly by the Federal Police and the Navy. Under the PEC, a Federal Waterway Police would join the public security bodies.

s8406896.titulo: Adds protection of security and health workers to the fundamental rights
s8406896.oQueMuda: States that protection of public security and health workers is guaranteed, as set by law. On its own, it does not say what that protection would be: a law is needed.
s8406896.quemAfeta: Police officers, firefighters, health workers and the government.
s8406896.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution has no specific right to protection for public security and health workers. Under the PEC, this right would be expressly stated, as set by law.

s8407865.titulo: Restricts appointments to state company boards
s8407865.oQueMuda: Bans appointing people with conflicts of interest to boards and management of state-owned companies.
s8407865.porQueImporta: Since 2016 the State Companies Law has banned appointing recent politicians and party leaders to run state companies. Under the PEC, rules against conflicts of interest in these appointments would be in the Constitution.

c2231670.titulo: Creates committees to reduce health lawsuits
c2231670.oQueMuda: States would have multi-agency committees to resolve health requests without going to court.
c2231670.quemAfeta: Patients, the public health system (SUS) and the judiciary.
c2231670.porQueImporta: Today patients who cannot get medicines or treatment from the public health system go to court, and there are hundreds of thousands of such cases. Under the PEC, each state would have committees to resolve these requests without a lawsuit.

s8220747.titulo: Lets all judges vote to elect court leadership
s8220747.oQueMuda: Court leadership (except the internal affairs office) would be elected by all tenured first- and second-instance judges in the region, by secret ballot, for 2-year terms.
s8220747.porQueImporta: Today court leadership is elected only by appellate judges. Under the PEC, all tenured judges, first and second instance, would vote by secret ballot, for 2-year terms.

s8221418.titulo: Allows converting hazardous work time to regular time for retirement
s8221418.oQueMuda: Social security contributors who worked in hazardous activities could convert that time into regular time.
s8221418.porQueImporta: Since the 2019 reform, people who worked exposed to health hazards cannot convert that special time into regular time to retire earlier. Under the PEC, conversion would be allowed again.

s8222502.titulo: Reserves women-only lists for court seats
s8222502.oQueMuda: One in every two nomination lists for the 'constitutional fifth' seats would be made up only of women.
s8222502.quemAfeta: Women lawyers, prosecutors and the courts.
s8222502.porQueImporta: Today the 'fifth' lists of lawyers and prosecutors for appeal courts have no gender reservation. Under the PEC, one in every two lists would include only women.

s8230006.oQueMuda: Donations of goods and services for humanitarian aid would be tax-free.
s8230006.porQueImporta: Today donations of goods and services pay taxes like ordinary sales, except for specific exemptions. Under the PEC, donations for humanitarian action would be tax-free.

s8394951.titulo: Alternates where provisional measures start between Chamber and Senate
s8394951.oQueMuda: Provisional measures would start alternately in the Chamber and the Senate, and joint committees would be abolished.
s8394951.porQueImporta: Today provisional measures go through a joint committee and start in the Chamber. Under the PEC, they would start alternately in the Chamber and Senate, without a joint committee.

c2132847.titulo: Sends work-related social security cases to the Labor Courts
c2132847.oQueMuda: Cases about work-related social security benefits, such as accidents, would go to the Labor Courts.
c2132847.quemAfeta: Injured workers and the national social security institute (INSS).
c2132847.porQueImporta: Today lawsuits against INSS over workplace accident benefits are tried by state courts. Under the PEC, they would go to the Labor Courts.

s7760703.titulo: Bans pardons for heinous and corruption crimes
s7760703.oQueMuda: The president could not pardon or commute sentences of people convicted of heinous or equivalent crimes, crimes against public administration, money laundering and crimes against the financial system.
s7760703.porQueImporta: Today the president cannot pardon heinous crimes, torture, trafficking and terrorism, but can pardon corruption and money laundering. Under the PEC, these would also be banned.

s8373076.titulo: Strengthens protection of final court rulings
s8373076.oQueMuda: Reaffirms that final rulings cannot be undone, including by changes in Supreme Court interpretation.
s8373076.quemAfeta: Taxpayers and parties to closed cases.
s8373076.porQueImporta: In 2023 the Supreme Court ruled that final decisions on taxes charged continuously lose effect when the court changes its view. Under the PEC, final decisions could not be undone by such changes.

c2222337.titulo: Shares pre-salt auction revenue with states and cities
c2222337.oQueMuda: From the money raised in auctions of the transfer-of-rights pre-salt surplus, minus the cost of revising the contract with Petrobras, the federal government would pass 15% to the states and the Federal District and 15% to municipalities, using the participation fund criteria.
c2222337.quemAfeta: States, cities and the federal government.
c2222337.porQueImporta: In 2019 another amendment (102) already authorized sharing part of the money from the pre-salt transfer-of-rights auction with states and municipalities. This PEC dealt with the same issue.

c2351620.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for loans to other countries
c2351620.oQueMuda: Federal public banks could only lend to foreign countries with Congress's authorization.
c2351620.quemAfeta: The BNDES and other public banks.
c2351620.porQueImporta: Today federal public banks can lend to other countries without congressional approval. Under the PEC, these loans would depend on lawmakers' authorization.

s1400311.titulo: Sets deadlines to appoint officials approved by the Senate
s1400311.oQueMuda: Creates deadlines to choose and appoint officials such as agency directors, with an impeachable offense if missed.
s1400311.porQueImporta: Today there is no deadline for the president to nominate or appoint officials after Senate approval, and agency posts stay vacant for months. Under the PEC, there would be deadlines, and missing them would be an impeachable offense.

s1401169.titulo: Requires a complementary law for concession rules
s1401169.oQueMuda: Public service concessions and permits would be regulated by a complementary law.
s1401169.quemAfeta: Concession holders and public service users.
s1401169.porQueImporta: Today public service concessions are regulated by ordinary law, passed by simple majority. Under the PEC, they would require a complementary law, which needs an absolute majority to pass or change.

s3037753.titulo: Changes how the Cide fuel tax is shared with states and cities
s3037753.oQueMuda: The shared portion of the fuel Cide would become 1/3 for states and the Federal District and 1/3 for municipalities, distributed by law, still earmarked for transport infrastructure.
s3037753.porQueImporta: Today 29% of the fuel Cide goes to states, which pass a quarter of it to municipalities (about 7% of the total). Under the PEC, states and municipalities would get two thirds of the revenue, and the federal government one third.

s7411048.titulo: Makes it easier to arrest and prosecute legislators
s7411048.oQueMuda:
Deputies and senators could be arrested in the act of a non-bailable crime, after a second-instance conviction, or under preventive or temporary detention when using their office to commit crimes.
The power of the Chamber and the Senate to suspend criminal cases against their members would end.
s7411048.porQueImporta: Today lawmakers can only be arrested when caught in the act of a non-bailable crime, and their house can vote to release them or suspend the case. Under the PEC, they could be imprisoned after an appeal-court conviction, and Congress would lose the power to block arrests and prosecutions.

s1401465.oQueMuda: Changes the system of government to parliamentarism, with a prime minister.
s1401465.porQueImporta: Today the elected president is both head of state and of government; in 1993 voters chose this system in a referendum. Under the PEC, a prime minister backed by Congress would head the government.

s1401414.titulo: Changes how attorneys general are chosen
s1401414.oQueMuda: The Prosecutor General could also come from state prosecutors' offices, and attorneys general would have to step down before seeking reappointment.
s1401414.porQueImporta: Today the Prosecutor General is chosen among federal prosecutors and can be reappointed without leaving office. Under the PEC, he or she could also come from state prosecution services, and anyone seeking reappointment would have to resign first.

s7914500.titulo: Creates a fixed term and list of three for the Federal Police chief
s7914500.oQueMuda: The Federal Police director would be chosen from a list of three, with a three-year term and Senate approval.
s7914500.quemAfeta: The Federal Police and the Presidency.
s7914500.porQueImporta: Today the Federal Police director is freely chosen by the president, with no fixed term. Under the PEC, he or she would come from a list of three names, serve a three-year term and need Senate approval.

s7989488.titulo: Requires officeholders to step down to seek reelection
s7989488.oQueMuda: The President, governors and mayors seeking reelection would have to take leave six months before.
s7989488.quemAfeta: Heads of the executive and voters.
s7989488.porQueImporta: Today the president, governors and mayors can run for re-election without leaving office. Under the PEC, they would have to step down six months before the election.

c2325720.titulo: Halves city governments' social security contributions
c2325720.oQueMuda: Cities would pay half the contribution rate on their payroll.
c2325720.porQueImporta: Today city governments pay INSS 20% of the payroll of staff without their own pension system. Under the PEC, they would pay half, and INSS would not receive the difference.

c501028.titulo: Allows using court-ordered government debts to buy a home
c501028.oQueMuda: Credits from court-ordered government debts (precatórios) could be used to buy a home.
c501028.porQueImporta: Today people owed court-ordered payments wait in the government's payment queue or sell the credit at a discount. Under the PEC, they could use it to buy a home.

s1401223.titulo: Guarantees women seats on Congress's governing boards and committees
s1401223.oQueMuda: The makeup of governing boards and committees would have to be proportional to the number of each gender.
s1401223.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution requires party proportionality in leadership boards and committees, but not gender proportionality. Under the PEC, composition would also have to reflect the number of men and women in the house.

s8392917.titulo: Alternates between the Chamber and the Senate where the president's proposals start
s8392917.oQueMuda:
The president's constitutional amendments, bills and provisional measures would start alternately in the Chamber and the Senate.
Bills from the Supreme Court, superior courts, the prosecutor-general and the public defender-general would still start in the Chamber.
s8392917.porQueImporta: Today the president's bills and provisional measures always start in the Chamber, which has the final say when the Senate changes the text. Under the PEC, the Senate would be the starting house in half the cases.

s8133142.titulo: Requires free, science-based public health care
s8133142.oQueMuda: Public health actions and services would have to be free and based on scientific evidence.
s8133142.quemAfeta: Patients of the public health system (SUS).
s8133142.porQueImporta: Today the public health system is free by law and there is no constitutional requirement of a scientific basis for its services. Under the PEC, public health services would have to be free and evidence-based, by constitutional rule.

s8171441.titulo: Sets rules for adding new treatments to the public health system
s8171441.oQueMuda: Creates criteria for adding new medicines and procedures to the SUS, with mandatory prior review.
s8171441.porQueImporta: Since 2011 a law has required review by Conitec before the public health system adopts new medicines and procedures. Under the PEC, criteria for adoption would be in the Constitution.

s1394077.titulo: Reserves legislative seats for people with disabilities
s1394077.oQueMuda: For the next four legislatures, people with disabilities would have a minimum share of seats in the Chamber of Deputies, state assemblies and city councils: 2.5% in the first, 5% in the second, 7.5% in the third and 10% in the fourth.
s1394077.porQueImporta: Today there are no reserved seats in legislatures for any group. Under the PEC, seats would be reserved for people with disabilities in the Chamber, state legislatures and city councils for four terms.

s1394130.titulo: Creates the Racial Equality Promotion Fund
s1394130.oQueMuda: Creates a fund for policies including Black Brazilians in housing, education and job training.
s1394130.porQueImporta: Today policies for Black Brazilians depend on each year's budget. Under the PEC, 1% of income tax and IPI would go to a Racial Equality Promotion Fund.

s1394231.titulo: Gives priority to bills on the same subject as provisional measures
s1394231.oQueMuda: Bills on the same topic as a provisional measure would be reviewed alongside it, with priority for the oldest.
s1394231.porQueImporta: Today provisional measures have priority and block the agenda, while lawmakers' bills on the same topic take a back seat. Under the PEC, they would be considered together with the measure, with priority to the older text.

s1394282.titulo: Creates national rules for public service exams
s1394282.oQueMuda: Exams would have to offer all open positions, and exams just for a waiting list or new exams with approved candidates still waiting would be banned.
s1394282.porQueImporta: Today public bodies can hold exams only for a reserve list and open new exams while approved candidates are waiting. Under the PEC, this would be banned, and all open positions would have to be offered.

s1394688.titulo: Extends special retirement rules for teachers in the transition
s1394688.oQueMuda: Basic education teachers would get five years off the requirements under the 2005 transition rule too.
s1394688.porQueImporta: Today basic education teachers have a five-year reduction under general rules, but not under one of the 2005 transition rules. Under the PEC, the reduction would also apply to that rule.

s1394843.titulo: Adjusts pensions by the most favorable inflation index
s1394843.oQueMuda: Social security benefits would be adjusted by the inflation index most favorable to retirees.
s1394843.quemAfeta: Retirees and pensioners of the national social security system.
s1394843.porQueImporta: Today INSS benefits are adjusted by the INPC, an inflation index set by law. Under the PEC, the inflation index giving retirees the largest raise would be used.

s1394997.titulo: Calls an assembly to carry out political reform
s1394997.oQueMuda: Voters would elect representatives to a review assembly devoted only to political and electoral reform.
s1394997.porQueImporta: Today changes to political and electoral rules are made by Congress itself. Under the PEC, voters would choose representatives for an assembly devoted only to political reform.

s1402212.oQueMuda: People not affiliated with parties could run in elections.
s1402212.porQueImporta: Today one can only run for office as a member of a party. Under the PEC, people without a party could also run.

s7242157.titulo: Automatically removes legislators convicted under the Clean Record Law
s7242157.oQueMuda: Deputies and senators convicted of crimes that cause ineligibility would lose their seats automatically.
s7242157.porQueImporta: Today a lawmaker convicted of a crime only loses the seat after a vote in the Chamber or Senate. Under the PEC, the loss would be automatic if the crime causes ineligibility under the Clean Record Law.

s7399577.titulo: Reserves 2% of legislators' amendments for sports
s7399577.oQueMuda: At least 2% of individual budget amendments would go to sports.
s7399577.porQueImporta: Today half of individual budget amendments must go to health, and the rest is free. Under the PEC, at least 2% would have to go to sport.

c1280152.titulo: Charges ICMS on interstate electricity sales
c1280152.oQueMuda: The ICMS would apply to electricity transactions between states.
c1280152.porQueImporta: Today electricity sold from one state to another pays no ICMS in the state of origin; the tax goes to the state where it is consumed. Under the PEC, the producing state would also charge ICMS on these sales.

c1594140.titulo: Allows reducing states' delegations in the Chamber
c1594140.oQueMuda: Ends the rule that prevents reducing the number of deputies from each state.
c1594140.porQueImporta: Today each state has between 8 and 70 federal deputies, and a rule prevents reducing a state's delegation. Under the PEC, this rule would end, and seats could be redistributed by population.

c609753.titulo: Federal aid to pay the nursing salary floor
c609753.oQueMuda:
Federal aid: the federal government gives financial support to states, municipalities, charities and private providers serving at least 60% of patients through SUS so they can pay the nursing minimum wage, with its own budget line.
Payroll limits: the extra spending on the minimum wage did not count toward payroll limits in the first year and is phased in, 10% a year.
Funding source: surpluses from federal public funds may pay the minimum wage from 2023 to 2027.
c609753.quemAfeta: Nursing professionals, municipalities, state governments, charity hospitals and hospitals serving SUS.
c609753.porQueImporta: In force since December 2022. The nursing minimum wage was created by law in 2022, but states, municipalities and hospitals said they could not afford it; the amendment set that the federal government helps pay.

c1701050.titulo: Bans creating costs for governments without naming a funding source
c1701050.oQueMuda: Laws could not impose costs on federal, state and city governments without provision in the budget.
c1701050.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 128 of 2022): federal laws cannot create expenses for states and municipalities without indicating where the money will come from.

c43596.titulo: Guarantees yearly funding for the Amazon and Northeast funds
c43596.oQueMuda: A law would set mandatory yearly amounts for these regions' development funds.
c43596.quemAfeta: Companies and governments in the Amazon and Northeast.
c43596.porQueImporta: Today the Amazon and Northeast development funds receive amounts set in each year's budget. Under the PEC, a law would set mandatory annual amounts.

c2194899.titulo: Takes federal university spending out of the cap (text of the Transition PEC)
c2194899.oQueMuda: Excludes federal education institutions' spending from the spending cap; in 2022 it was the text used to vote on the Transition PEC.
c2194899.porQueImporta: In 2022 this text was used in the Chamber to vote on the Transition PEC, which allowed spending outside the cap in 2023, such as the R$600 Bolsa Família. The original proposal removed federal university spending from the cap.

c620527.oQueMuda:
The federal government, states and municipalities would have to spend a minimum every year on cultural heritage and on producing and spreading culture: 2% of federal tax revenue, 1.5% of state revenue (including the participation fund) and 1% of municipal revenue.
Part of the federal money would go to states and municipalities.
Failing to spend the minimum could lead to intervention, as already happens with health and education.
c620527.porQueImporta: Today health and education have mandatory minimum spending, but culture does not. Under the PEC, the federal government, states and the Federal District would have to spend a minimum share of revenue on culture.

c2095531.titulo: Adds reciprocity to the principles of foreign policy
c2095531.oQueMuda: Adds 'reciprocity' (treating other countries as they treat Brazil) to the list of principles of international relations. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2095531.quemAfeta: The federal government, diplomacy and Brazilians abroad.
c2095531.porQueImporta: Today the foreign policy principles in the Constitution include national independence, human rights and non-intervention, but not reciprocity. Under the PEC, reciprocity would be added.

c2194813.oQueMuda: Cooking gas for household use would be tax-free.
c2194813.porQueImporta: Today cooking gas pays ICMS and other taxes. Under the PEC, gas for household use would be tax-free, and states and the federal government would stop collecting on it.

c2230007.titulo: Guarantees income for families in poverty
c2230007.oQueMuda: Social assistance would have to guarantee cash transfers to poor and extremely poor families.
c2230007.porQueImporta: Today Bolsa Família exists by law, and the Constitution has provided a family basic income since 2021. Under the PEC, social assistance would have the duty to guarantee cash transfers to poor and extremely poor families.

c2285501.titulo: Let cities pay pension debts in 240 installments
c2285501.oQueMuda: In 2021, cities could pay their social security debts in up to 240 monthly installments.
c2285501.porQueImporta: In 2021, municipalities gained the option to pay pension debts in up to 240 months. This PEC deals with that installment plan.

c2304959.titulo: Puts climate security into the Constitution
c2304959.oQueMuda: Adds 'climate security' to the fundamental rights and to the principles of the economy, and tells the government to act against climate change and its effects. It does not say which actions nor create funding.
c2304959.quemAfeta: The whole population, companies and governments.
c2304959.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution guarantees an ecologically balanced environment, without mentioning climate. Under the PEC, climate security would be added to fundamental rights and economic principles, and governments would have a duty to act against climate change.

c2336964.titulo: Federal aid to pay the nursing minimum wage
c2336964.oQueMuda: The federal government would give financial support to states, cities and charities to meet the nursing minimum salary.
c2336964.porQueImporta: This proposal was shelved; federal aid to pay the nursing salary floor entered the Constitution in 2022 through another PEC (Amendment 127).

s7728717.titulo: Adds the National Force to the public safety bodies
s7728717.oQueMuda: The National Public Safety Force would be a permanent body for cooperation among governments.
s7728717.quemAfeta: The National Force and the states.
s7728717.porQueImporta: Today the National Public Security Force exists by decree and law and acts when states request support. Under the PEC, it would be a permanent body in the Constitution.

s7732135.titulo: Separates electoral crimes from ordinary crimes in court cases
s7732135.oQueMuda: Ordinary crimes linked to electoral crimes would be tried by the regular courts.
s7732135.quemAfeta: Defendants in corruption and slush-fund cases.
s7732135.porQueImporta: Since 2019, under a Supreme Court ruling, ordinary crimes linked to electoral crimes, such as corruption tied to illegal campaign funds, are tried by Electoral Courts. Under the PEC, they would go to ordinary courts.

s7733509.titulo: Allows holding two public journalist jobs
s7733509.oQueMuda: Journalists could hold two public posts with compatible hours.
s7733509.porQueImporta: Today civil servants can only hold two public posts in listed cases, such as teachers and health professionals. Under the PEC, journalists could too.

s7738877.oQueMuda:
The president could issue at most five provisional measures per legislative year, valid for 30 days, extendable by another 30.
Measures on labor law, on matters already covered by a pending bill and on different topics in the same measure would be banned.
Amendments unrelated to the measure would be banned and could be rejected outright.
Provisional measures would no longer block Congress's agenda.
s7738877.porQueImporta: Today there is no limit on the number of provisional measures, which last up to 120 days and block the agenda after 45. Under the PEC, there would be a limit of five a year and a shorter term.

s7741158.titulo: Requires technical selection of federal audit court ministers
s7741158.oQueMuda: Federal audit court ministers would be chosen from auditors and prosecutors with no recent elected office.
s7741158.porQueImporta: Today of the 9 Federal Audit Court ministers, 6 are chosen by Congress and 3 by the president, and many were politicians. Under the PEC, they would be chosen among audit court auditors and prosecutors, without recent elected office.

s7745408.titulo: Ends 60-day vacations and allows judges to be dismissed
s7745408.oQueMuda: Judges and prosecutors would have 30 days of vacation, would not be punished with retirement and could be dismissed.
s7745408.porQueImporta: Today judges and prosecutors have 60 days of vacation, and the maximum administrative penalty is compulsory retirement with proportional pay. Under the PEC, they would have 30 days of vacation and could lose their post as punishment.

s7748831.titulo: Allows public universities to charge for services
s7748831.oQueMuda: Universities could charge for services they provide and manage their own revenue.
s7748831.porQueImporta: Today money federal universities earn from services goes into the federal budget and can be frozen. Under the PEC, they could charge for services and manage these funds themselves.

s7752601.titulo: Moves the rural land tax to the municipalities
s7752601.oQueMuda: Cities would collect the rural land tax (ITR), now charged by the federal government.
s7752601.porQueImporta: Today the ITR rural land tax is federal, and half goes to the municipality, or all of it if the municipality handles collection. Under the PEC, the tax would become municipal.

s7753619.titulo: Caps interest rates charged by banks
s7753619.oQueMuda: Banks could not charge more than three times the Selic benchmark rate.
s7753619.porQueImporta: Today there is no limit on bank interest rates, and revolving credit card and overdraft rates are among the highest in the world. Under the PEC, no rate could exceed three times the Selic rate.

s7759040.titulo: Adjusts federal transfers to cities for inflation
s7759040.oQueMuda: Balances of federal programs with cities would be updated for inflation every year.
s7759040.porQueImporta: Today balances of federal programs with municipalities have fixed values, without automatic adjustment. Under the PEC, they would be adjusted for inflation every year.

s7759495.titulo: Requires drug testing of police and firefighters
s7759495.oQueMuda: Public safety professionals would undergo periodic drug testing.
s7759495.porQueImporta: Today professional truck and bus drivers already take drug tests, but there is no national rule for police and firefighters. Under the PEC, they would take periodic drug tests.

s7774325.oQueMuda: Products made mainly from recycled material would be tax-free.
s7774325.porQueImporta: Today recycled products pay taxes like any others. Under the PEC, products made mainly with recycled material would be tax-free.

s7775664.titulo: Bans reissuing decrees struck down by Congress
s7775664.oQueMuda: The government could not reissue, in the same year, a decree halted by Congress.
s7775664.porQueImporta: Today Congress can suspend a presidential decree, but the government can issue a similar one. Under the PEC, reissuing a suspended decree in the same year would be banned.

s7775894.titulo: Raises to 28% the share of Income Tax and IPI going to the FPM
s7775894.oQueMuda: The main share of Income Tax and IPI allocated to the Municipal Participation Fund would rise from 22.5% to 28%, gradually: 23.5% in the first year, 24.5% in the second, 25.5% in the third, until reaching 28%.
s7775894.porQueImporta: Today FPM receives 22.5% of income tax and IPI, plus extra 1% shares in three months of the year. Under the PEC, it would receive 5.5 percentage points more, and the federal government would keep less.

s7786111.oQueMuda: Mayors and council members elected in 2020 would serve six years to unify elections in 2026.
s7786111.porQueImporta: Today municipal and general elections alternate every two years. Under the PEC, mayors and councilors elected in 2020 would have 6-year terms, with no election in 2024, to unify the calendar in 2026.

s7798303.titulo: Removes public investment from the spending cap
s7798303.oQueMuda: Federal public investment and other spending that adds to fixed capital, including the Minha Casa Minha Vida housing program, would be outside the spending cap up to 1.5% of GDP, with mandatory execution.
s7798303.porQueImporta: In 2019 the 2016 spending cap limited all federal spending, including investment. Under the PEC, investment up to 1.5% of GDP would be outside that limit. The cap was replaced in 2023 by another fiscal rule.

s7811689.titulo: Allows endowment funds for federal universities
s7811689.oQueMuda:
Public universities could create endowment funds, from donations, to support teaching and research, without using them to pay salaries.
Donors could deduct from federal taxes up to 5% (individuals) or 2% (companies) of the annual amount owed.
s7811689.porQueImporta: Since 2019 a law has allowed endowment funds with donations for universities, with no tax benefit for donors. Under the PEC, these funds would have a constitutional basis and donors would get tax deductions.

s7822485.titulo: Uses regional funds for state and city infrastructure
s7822485.oQueMuda: For five years, 30% of the North, Northeast and Center-West funds would go to infrastructure works.
s7822485.quemAfeta: States and cities in these regions.
s7822485.porQueImporta: Today the North, Northeast and Center-West constitutional funds lend money to companies and producers. Under the PEC, for five years, 30% of that money would go to state and municipal infrastructure works.

s7822487.titulo: Compensates states and cities hosting rocket launch bases
s7822487.oQueMuda: Places with aerospace launch centers would receive compensation and a social fund.
s7822487.quemAfeta: Residents of Alcântara (Maranhão) and the surrounding region.
s7822487.porQueImporta: Today there is no specific compensation for states and municipalities hosting rocket launch centers, such as Alcântara in Maranhão. Under the PEC, they would receive financial compensation and a social fund.

s7828021.titulo: Protects pregnant civil servants in appointed posts
s7828021.oQueMuda: Women in appointed posts could not be dismissed from pregnancy until five months after birth.
s7828021.quemAfeta: Women civil servants in appointed posts.
s7828021.porQueImporta: Today formally employed women and tenured civil servants have job stability from pregnancy until five months after birth; for appointees, the guarantee comes from a Supreme Court ruling. Under the PEC, this protection would be in the Constitution.

s7845448.titulo: Creates a national fund for environmental emergencies
s7845448.oQueMuda:
A National Fund for Environmental Emergencies would be created, paid for with part of the royalties and compensation from oil and natural gas extraction.
The government would have a duty to keep a fund to deal with environmental emergencies.
s7845448.quemAfeta: Coastal residents and people in risk areas.
s7845448.porQueImporta: Today money for environmental disasters, like the 2019 oil spill on the Northeast coast, comes from each year's budget. Under the PEC, there would be a dedicated fund, fed by oil extraction.

s7971591.titulo: Adds fighting corruption to the foundations of the Republic
s7971591.oQueMuda: Adds 'preventing and fighting corruption' to the country's foundations, alongside sovereignty, citizenship and human dignity. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s7971591.quemAfeta: The whole population, public bodies and lawmakers.
s7971591.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution requires integrity in public administration, but fighting corruption is not among the foundations of the Republic, which are sovereignty, citizenship, human dignity, the value of work and political pluralism. Under the PEC, it would be added.

s8153922.titulo: Lets legislators become ambassadors without losing their seats
s8153922.oQueMuda: Deputies and senators could head embassies without losing their seats.
s8153922.porQueImporta: Today deputies and senators can only step aside without losing their seat to become ministers, secretaries or heads of temporary diplomatic missions. Under the PEC, they could head permanent embassies.

s8228548.titulo: Bans handing public forest land to private parties
s8228548.oQueMuda:
Granting title to private individuals or companies over public land covered by forest or native vegetation, even if regenerating, and converting it to other uses would be banned; clearing the area would not lift the ban.
These lands would have to become, by December 31, 2026, protected areas, Indigenous lands, forest concessions or use concessions to traditional peoples and communities.
s8228548.quemAfeta: Forest communities, governments and land occupants.
s8228548.porQueImporta: Today millions of hectares of public forests have no defined use and are frequent targets of land grabbing and deforestation. Under the PEC, these areas could not be titled to private parties and would have a deadline to be assigned.

s7711916.titulo: Requires open votes to elect Congress's leadership
s7711916.oQueMuda: The speakers of the Chamber and the Senate would be chosen by open vote.
s7711916.porQueImporta: Today the heads of the Chamber and Senate are elected by secret ballot. Under the PEC, the vote would be open, and voters would know whom each lawmaker voted for.

s7717123.titulo: Ends the benefit for prisoners' families
s7717123.oQueMuda: The benefit paid to prisoners' dependents would end.
s7717123.porQueImporta: Today the prisoner's family benefit is paid to dependents of low-income prisoners who contributed to INSS. Under the PEC, this benefit would cease to exist.

s7717281.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 16
s7717281.oQueMuda: Only people under 16 would be exempt from criminal responsibility.
s7717281.quemAfeta: Teenagers aged 16 and 17 and the justice system.
s7717281.porQueImporta: Today people under 18 are subject to the Child and Adolescent Statute, with at most 3 years of detention. Under the PEC, 16- and 17-year-olds would be tried and imprisoned as adults.

s7718602.titulo: Allows imprisonment after a second-instance conviction
s7718602.oQueMuda: Sentences would start after conviction by an appeals court, even with appeals pending.
s7718602.porQueImporta: Today, under a 2019 Supreme Court ruling, a sentence only begins after all appeals are exhausted. Under the PEC, it would begin after conviction by an appeal court.

s7724131.titulo: Counts military service in police entrance exams
s7724131.oQueMuda: Mandatory military service would count as a credential or tiebreaker in exams for police, firefighters and municipal guards.
s7724131.porQueImporta: Today police, firefighter and guard exams give no points for military service, except under each notice's rules. Under the PEC, compulsory military service would count as a credential or tiebreaker.

s7726829.titulo: Punishes trading posts for political advantage
s7726829.oQueMuda: Appointing or dismissing people to gain political advantage or influence another branch would be misconduct.
s7726829.porQueImporta: Today the Administrative Misconduct Law does not specifically cover appointing or dismissing someone for political advantage. Under the PEC, this conduct would be misconduct, with penalties such as loss of office and political rights.

s7728643.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 15 for serious crimes
s7728643.oQueMuda: Young people aged 15 to 17 could be tried as adults for serious crimes, based on a judge's assessment.
s7728643.porQueImporta: Today people under 18 are subject to the Child and Adolescent Statute, with at most 3 years of detention. Under the PEC, 15- to 17-year-olds could be tried as adults for serious crimes, at the judge's discretion.

s7730777.titulo: Changes how ICMS is split among cities
s7730777.oQueMuda: Lowers from 75% to 50% the share of ICMS split according to each city's economic activity.
s7730777.porQueImporta: Today 25% of ICMS goes to municipalities, and at least 65% of that share is split by each town's economic activity (75% until 2020). Under this 2019 PEC, that criterion would drop to 50%, with the rest following each state's rules.

s7731793.oQueMuda: Only parties with 5% of the vote for the Chamber or 20 deputies would be represented in Congress.
s7731793.porQueImporta: Since 2017 there has been a gradual performance threshold that by 2030 will require 3% of Chamber votes or 15 deputies for a party to get public funds and TV time. Under the PEC, only parties with 5% of votes or 20 deputies would be represented in Congress.

s7733746.oQueMuda: Merit-based promotion of judges would consider the top half of the seniority list.
s7733746.porQueImporta: Today, in merit-based promotions, judges in the first fifth of the seniority list compete. Under the PEC, the first half of the list would compete.

s7733785.titulo: Makes the Fundeb education fund permanent
s7733785.oQueMuda: The main fund financing basic education would no longer have an end date.
s7733785.porQueImporta: Already in force through another PEC (Amendment 108 of 2020): Fundeb, which pays much of teachers' salaries, became permanent, with a gradual increase in the federal share.

s7737914.titulo: Takes public investment out of the spending cap
s7737914.oQueMuda: Investment spending would not count toward the spending cap.
s7737914.quemAfeta: The federal government and public works sectors.
s7737914.porQueImporta: This 2019 PEC proposed removing public investment from the spending cap created in 2016. The cap was eventually replaced in 2023 by another fiscal rule.

s7738872.titulo: Guarantees minimum federal funding for public safety
s7738872.oQueMuda: The federal government would spend increasing amounts on the Unified Public Safety System, up to 2.5% of its revenue.
s7738872.porQueImporta: Today public security has no mandatory federal minimum spending. Under the PEC, the federal government would spend growing amounts on the Unified Public Security System, up to 2.5% of its revenue.

s7741423.titulo: Requires a list of three to choose the Prosecutor General
s7741423.oQueMuda: The Prosecutor General would be chosen from a list drawn up by members of the prosecution service.
s7741423.porQueImporta: Today the president freely chooses the Prosecutor General among career prosecutors, with Senate approval. Under the PEC, the choice would have to come from a list voted by prosecutors.

s7741529.titulo: Bans special pension plans for politicians
s7741529.oQueMuda: There could be no separate retirement systems for elected officials.
s7741529.porQueImporta: Since the 2019 reform, new lawmakers cannot join Congress's own pension plan. Under the PEC, no special retirement regime for elected officials could exist.

s7741534.oQueMuda: Repeals Amendment 95, which created the public spending cap.
s7741534.quemAfeta: The federal government and public policies.
s7741534.porQueImporta: This 2019 PEC proposed repealing the spending cap created in 2016. The cap was eventually replaced in 2023 by another fiscal rule.
